identity.title: Optimal Mistake Bounds for Transductive Online Learning

problem.claim: Quantify the difference between transductive and standard online learning, especially the power of unlabeled data.

gap.claim: The abstract presents this as a 30-year-old open problem, with prior transductive lower bounds substantially below the claimed bound.

contributions.claim: Proves an Ω(√d) transductive mistake bound for every concept class with Littlestone dimension d.
Shows tightness by exhibiting, for every d, a class of Littlestone dimension d with transductive mistake bound O(√d).
Improves the previous best stated upper bound of (2/3)·d and identifies a quadratic gap between transductive and standard online learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they resolve the open problem by tightly quantifying the transductive-versus-standard online-learning gap.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an Ω(√d) lower bound for every concept class of Littlestone dimension d.
The authors report matching O(√d) transductive mistake bounds for a class at every dimension d.
The authors report that this improves prior lower bounds of Ω(log log d), Ω(√log d), and Ω(log d), and the prior upper bound (2/3)·d.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames the power of unlabeled data in online learning as a long-standing open problem.
It establishes an Ω(√d) transductive mistake bound for every class with Littlestone dimension d.
It reports a matching O(√d) construction and improvement over earlier bounds.
The results are presented as a quadratic transductive-versus-standard gap, contrasting with similar complexities in PAC learning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a universal lower bound with a dimension-by-dimension matching construction before drawing the gap conclusion.

lessons.interpretation: This aligns a broad impossibility-style statement with a concrete tightness witness, making the scope of the characterization easier to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a rate characterization, pair a universal bound with an explicit matching construction or state precisely where tightness is unavailable.
lessons.exception: This pattern is unsuitable when matching instances are impossible, irrelevant to the task, or would distract from a genuinely instance-specific result.

unknowns: The abstract does not define the transductive mistake-bound model or the precise standard-learning benchmark used for the quadratic-gap claim.
Proof details, construction details, and conditions behind the PAC comparison are not supplied.
The abstract does not provide numerical constants or finite-sample qualifications for the asymptotic bounds.
